chunks: "I measure current for four main reasons. First, protection.
Current is what overheats and destroys things, so I want a fast overcurrent limit to shut down on a short or stall before a FET, trace or connector cooks. Second, control.
In a switching converter, peak-current-mode control senses inductor current every cycle for faster response and automatic current limiting.
In a motor driver, current is proportional to torque, so closing a current loop gives me torque control and smooth start-up. Third, monitoring.
A battery management system integrates current over time to estimate state of charge, and a power monitor multiplies it by voltage to report watts for power budgeting, thermal management, or billing.
Fourth, diagnostics. Current tells me whether a load is connected, if a motor is stalled, if a sensor is shorted, or if a channel has degraded, which voltage alone often can't.
The reason shapes the sensor: protection needs speed, metering needs accuracy and low offset drift, control needs bandwidth and linearity."
